inspiration: test_tail_tail_bytes_ret_dup; angr CFG call-graph no-return analysis (undefined-extern __stack_chk_fail); tail_bytes
root_cause: In an ELF relocatable object (ET_REL .o) __stack_chk_fail is an UNDEFINED external symbol (UND, NOTYPE, size 0, no address). kuna's analysis-tier known-no-return pass (noreturn_known, default on) keys its facts on the ADDRESS of a *defined* FUNC symbol, so it never marks the UND extern -- even though its base name (stack_chk_fail) is on the shipped ElfFunctionsThatDoNotReturn list. At decompile flow time the call resolves to a display name but the symbol's no-return flag is false, so FlowEnvironment::query_call_no_return returns false, no artificialHalt(noreturn) is planted, and flow runs off the function's end into the next function. tail.o::tail_bytes (615 bytes, 0x401e80..0x4020e7) renders 326 lines / 9 gotos swallowing neighbour functions (tail_lines/die_pipe), vs angr's 96 lines / 1 goto. Manual 'option noreturn __stack_chk_fail' chops it 328 -> 87 lines, confirming the mechanism.
owning_stage: S2 flow classification: the FlowEnvironment::query_call_no_return seam (infra/decompile_drive.rs), consumed by FlowInfo at s2_lift/flow.rs query_call_no_return / checkForFlowModification (plants the artificial halt).
mechanism: Name-based no-return fallback in the flow seam ArchFlowEnv::query_call_no_return: when the address-keyed no-return check returns false AND the gate (Architecture flag noreturn_extern_calls) is on, resolve the callee display name (query_call) and return true if kuna_noreturnextern::matches_noreturn_extern_name matches the known ELF no-return list (mirrors the analysis-tier name_matches: leading-_ strip + std-only namespace guard, exact match against a closed name set). Plants the existing artificialHalt(noreturn) so flow stops at the call. New module kuna_noreturnextern.rs (ElementId 4103), Architecture flag modelled on tail_call_jumps. No new pass type, no S7 change.
kept_opt_in_reason: The name-based no-return match overlaps noreturn_known's name match for *defined/imported* symbols, so default-on changes PE/ELF exit-family handling under `option noreturn_known off`: verify_multiformat_passes::pe_exit_eliminates_dead_code_via_noreturn_list asserts that turning noreturn_known off restores the dead fall-through after a PE `exit`, but the fallback independently catches `exit`. The bytechunk-only 675-datatest corpus never exercises this (clean 0/675 ablation), but make rust-test caught it. Shipped default-off opt-in (no DIV), like tailcalljump/gotoreduce/stackguard; the .o undefined-extern fix is available via `option noreturn_extern on`.

decisions.question: Is closing this gap a small (one option-gated seam-gate) or large (proposal) feature, and is the flow-seam name-fallback the right layer vs an analysis-tier UND-scan?

risks: A user-defined function legitimately named after a known-noreturn libc symbol (e.g. a local exit that actually returns) could be wrongly truncated.
Name-matching is heuristic and could fire on an unrelated symbol that happens to share a known-noreturn name across an unexpected namespace.
Default-OFF gating means the garbage output persists for any user who does not know to flip the option (discoverability, not correctness).
mitigations: Gate fires ONLY when the existing symbol-address noreturn check already returned false, so any callee already marked noreturn is unaffected; keep the std-only namespace guard so user code in other namespaces never matches.
Ship default-OFF and require a clean ablation over the 675 datatests plus speed-in-budget before any consideration of default-on.
Leading-underscore stripping + an explicit closed name list (no fuzzy/substring match) bounds the matched surface; add the new stage test pinning tail_bytes to 87 lines to lock behavior.
decider_verdict.rationale: This is a single gated predicate added to an existing FlowEnvironment method (query_call_no_return), directly analogous to the established tail_call_jumps flow-seam gate -- no new pass type, no S7 structuring change, exactly 3 ported-core anchor files (architecture.rs, decompile_drive.rs, options.rs) plus non-core stages.toml, and one new module, so it sits inside every Hard-Rule-7 bound. The decompiler flow-time seam is the correct layer precisely because it stays option-gated, isolated, and opt-in, whereas the analysis-tier UND-scan alternative would be default-on and broader in blast radius. The manual 'option noreturn __stack_chk_fail' proof (328->87 lines) confirms the mechanism, and the fallback-only firing plus namespace guard contain the truncation risk.

decisions.outcome: Implemented as a small feature, shipped DEFAULT-OFF opt-in (matching the decider's conservative recommendation). The 675-datatest ablation with the gate on was clean (0/675) and the target was 37% faster, which first suggested default-ON + a DIV entry — but `make rust-test` caught a real interaction the bytechunk-only 675 corpus cannot exercise: verify_multiformat_passes::pe_exit_eliminates_dead_code_via_noreturn_list asserts `option noreturn_known off` restores the dead fall-through after a PE `exit`, yet the name-based fallback independently catches `exit`, so default-on would silently change PE/ELF exit-family handling under noreturn_known off. The name match overlaps noreturn_known's for defined/imported symbols, so the honest call is opt-in (no DIV); the .o undefined-extern fix is available via `option noreturn_extern on`.
